commands.step: Name it by the launcher's convention
commands.text:
VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
mkdir -p out
mv "dist/facet${{ matrix.ext }}" "out/facet-${VERSION}-${{ matrix.label }}${{ matrix.ext }}"
ls -l out/

commands.step: Smoke-test the binary before it can ever reach a user
commands.text:
VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
BIN="out/facet-${VERSION}-${{ matrix.label }}${{ matrix.ext }}"
chmod +x "$BIN" || true
"$BIN" --print-tools

commands.step: Verify tag matches every declared version
commands.text:
TAG="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
PYPROJECT=$(python -c "import tomllib,pathlib;print(tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text())['project']['version'])")
PKGJSON=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
# Extracted with python, NOT a node one-liner. The obvious node version
# uses a regex replacement containing $1, and bash expands $1 inside
# double quotes to an empty positional parameter - the JSON.parse then
# dies and takes the whole release with it. Caught in pre-flight.
BINJS=$(python -c "import re,pathlib;print(re.search(r'version:\s*\"([^\"]+)\"', pathlib.Path('bin/facet.js').read_text()).group(1))")
BINTAG=$(python -c "import re,pathlib;print(re.search(r'tag:\s*\"([^\"]+)\"', pathlib.Path('bin/facet.js').read_text()).group(1))")
if [ "$BINTAG" != "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" ]; then
  echo "::error::bin/facet.js pins tag $BINTAG but this release is $GITHUB_REF_NAME - npm-launcher would fetch the wrong release"
  exit 1
fi
SERVER=$(python -c "import re,pathlib;print(re.search(r'SERVER_VERSION = \"([^\"]+)\"', pathlib.Path('tools/record_mcp.py').read_text()).group(1))")
echo "tag=$TAG pyproject=$PYPROJECT package.json=$PKGJSON bin/facet.js=$BINJS record_mcp=$SERVER"
fail=0
for pair in "pyproject:$PYPROJECT" "package.json:$PKGJSON" "bin/facet.js:$BINJS" "record_mcp.py:$SERVER"; do
  name="${pair%%:*}"; val="${pair#*:}"
  if [ "$val" != "$TAG" ]; then echo "::error::$name declares $val but the tag is $TAG"; fail=1; fi
done
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

commands.step: Verify the wheel runs from a clean venv
commands.text:
set -euo pipefail
python -m venv /tmp/verify
/tmp/verify/bin/pip install --quiet dist/*.whl

# the floor: what this step used to be, in full
/tmp/verify/bin/facet-index --help > /dev/null
/tmp/verify/bin/facet-mcp --print-tools > /dev/null

# A VERB THAT TOUCHES THE CORPUS. `build` is the one that died with
# FileNotFoundError on <venv>/Lib/docs/experiments. It writes to a
# scratch path so the tracked index is never the thing under test.
/tmp/verify/bin/facet-index build --db /tmp/verify/index.db > /dev/null

# A VERB THAT TOUCHES THE DB, with no --db, which is how the default
# gets exercised at all. This exited 2 with "unable to open database
# file" on every published wheel.
/tmp/verify/bin/facet-index q erosion > /dev/null

# THE REFUSAL, from a directory that is not the record: 4 = REFUSED
# (E21 Ruling 4). A non-zero here is not enough - 2 is what the DEFECT
# returned, so this asserts the exact code.
rc=0
( cd /tmp && /tmp/verify/bin/facet-index build ) > /dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
if [ "$rc" -ne 4 ]; then
  echo "expected 4 = REFUSED outside a checkout, got $rc" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# And the server's own banner must name a path inside this checkout.
# The 0.1.0 binary printed a path under its extraction dir and exited
# 0; the wheel printed one under <venv>/Lib and exited 0.
db=$(/tmp/verify/bin/facet-mcp --print-tools | sed -n 's/^db: *//p' | head -1)
case "$db" in
  "$PWD"/*) ;;
  *) echo "the banner names a path outside the checkout: $db" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
echo "verbs run, the refusal returns 4, and the banner names $db"

commands.step: Cut the GitHub Release with binaries + dists
Install npm >=11.5 in a sandbox for OIDC
commands.text:
SANDBOX="$HOME/.npm-cli-sandbox"
mkdir -p "$SANDBOX"
pushd "$SANDBOX" >/dev/null
echo '{"name":"npm-cli-sandbox","version":"0.0.0","private":true}' > package.json
npm install --no-save --no-audit --no-fund --silent npm@latest
popd >/dev/null
echo "$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
"$SANDBOX/node_modules/.bin/npm" --version
